about.title: Personal Injury Help in Tulare, California
about.longDescription: Tulare sees its share of everyday traffic risk, with 51 injury collisions and 63 people hurt in the most recent final crash year, including one traffic death. Corridors like Rt 137, Blackstone, Bardsley, and SR-99 carry heavy local traffic, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. when commuters, shoppers, and weekend travelers overlap on the same roads. If you or someone you love was hurt in a collision on one of these corridors, or anywhere else in Tulare County, it helps to understand your options quickly, since California generally gives injured people two years to file a claim, and that window can shrink to as little as six months when a government entity is involved. We handle personal injury cases and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We'll review what happened and explain your options, no pressure, no obligation.

items.title: Two-Year Filing Window
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, but that timeline shrinks significantly if a government agency is involved, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still be able to recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic harm, unlike some other states.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning you pay nothing upfront and owe no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an injury in Tulare?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the incident to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity or vehicle was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your specific situation promptly.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Tulare?
items.answer: Public crash records show that reported collisions in Tulare are concentrated along corridors like Rt 137, Blackstone, Bardsley, and SR-99, with activity often peaking on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for what happened. Your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it wouldn't be barred outright.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation when you reach out.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much compensation I can receive?
items.answer: For most ordinary personal injury cases in California, there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. Every case is different, though, so we can review your specific circumstances.
